draft_evidence.quote: The next day was the one the mountain kept. Seln went at first light with the pack on and came back before the sun was over the gorge: the lip held a walker, and below the lip the fan the herd had taken down was still going, in slides, one every hundred breaths or so, and a man on it was a stone on it. "Tomorrow," he said, "or it's two of us." Nobody argued. The day was rationing and the leg. Karis woke and could not light a lamp and did not try a second time. Lira's leg went hot under the plates by noon, and the tape came off and went back on wetted, and she said nothing about it, which was how Cael knew. He counted breaths, and the slides on the fan, and the gorge, and did not take the log out.
